lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Linh, it's Daniela. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Daniela. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walking went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about whether coffee breaks the fast.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How have you been feeling since we last talked?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay. The heat is getting to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I did it! 3 out of 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you use the step counter?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, sometimes. I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You just weren't feeling it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to walk 10 minutes on 4 days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 3 out of 3 days, the hard part was the heat, and next week you're going to walk 10 minutes on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Linh, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

Self-efficacy and mood benefit; not reflected
Reflects preference for small, sustainable steps
Desire to regain energy; not explored

Sets goal for participant without collaboration
Names a barrier-solving plan: morning walk

flags.reason: Heat and fatigue reported in a cancer survivor; not explored for heat illness or energy concerns before moving on.
'You need to walk every day, no excuses' pushes and shames after participant expressed ambivalence.
Goal imposed without asking; participant replied 'I guess', signaling low buy-in.
'I want to get my energy back' and line 43 desire to feel like myself were not reflected or explored.
Coffee-and-fasting question was raised first and never addressed or deferred.

score.summary: The coach covered the call structure and set a next contact, but the goal was largely imposed, including a 'no excuses' directive at line 29 and a 4-day target at line 44 that the participant met with 'I guess'. Heat and fatigue were raised but not explored, and several strong change-talk statements went unreflected.
strengths: Affirmed persistence on a hard week (line 12) and planning ahead (line 27).
Asked permission before offering the walking-bout idea (line 40), a good MI move.
Ended with a clear summary and a confirmed next contact (lines 48-50).
coaching_tips: Replace the directive at line 29 with a reflection, e.g., 'Part of you wants to keep up, and part of you is really tired.'
Before setting the 4-day goal at line 44, ask 'What feels doable for you next week?' to build collaboration.
Explore the heat and fatigue from line 6 further, asking about hydration, timing, and when to contact the care team.
Reflect change talk such as lines 39 and 43 ('You want your energy back') and ask what that would look like.
